traceability.notes:
docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md is a concrete specification story, not a high-level map.
All acceptance criteria and listed requirements for this story are implemented and verified:
- Core functionality: `require-story-annotation` and `valid-annotation-format` both declare `meta.fixable = "code"` and provide ESLint fixers. tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts uses RuleTester with `--fix` expectations to confirm missing @story insertion and safe @story path suffix normalization. - Quality & safety: Fixers only insert JSDoc comments or adjust the `@story` path substring; helper logic (`createAddStoryFix`, `createMethodFix`, `createStoryFix`) ensures no runtime code is modified and surrounding formatting is preserved. When a safe range cannot be determined, the code falls back to reporting without a fix. - Idempotence & single application: Dedicated tests under the “[REQ-AUTOFIX-IDEMPOTENT] and [REQ-AUTOFIX-SINGLE-APPLICATION]” suites assert that after the first fix, subsequent `--fix` runs produce no further changes for both rules, and that suffix normalization is applied exactly once per path. - Selective control & templates: `require-story-annotation` supports `annotationTemplate`, `methodAnnotationTemplate`, and `autoFix` options, wired through `require-story-visitors` and `require-story-helpers`; tests confirm custom templates are used and that `autoFix: false` disables automatic insertion while still reporting errors. `valid-annotation-format` has a global `autoFix` option resolved in `valid-annotation-options.ts`, used in `validateStoryAnnotation` to disable suffix fixes while still validating. - Error handling: `createStoryFix` defends against missing tags or unlocatable values and returns null in such cases, causing `reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix` to degrade gracefully to non-fixing error reporting. The surrounding validation functions maintain this conservative behavior, so ambiguous or unsafe cases are not auto-fixed. - Documentation: user-docs/api-reference.md documents the `--fix` behavior, safety constraints, and configuration options for both rules, matching what the story requires. - Tests: All jest test suites, including tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts, pass in the latest run.
Based on the concrete implementation and passing, story-linked tests, the story docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md is fully implemented and remains in a PASSED state.
